g.text: Kao: a jar estimate before and after a social cue
602 people estimated a jar containing 659 objects, then could revise after seeing a number presented as other people's average.
Their guesses are real. The displayed social number was computer-generated; participants were not interacting with each other.
Kao et al. (2018) | doi.org/10.1098/rsif.2018.0130 | Data: figshare file 11094635 | 602 measured response pairs
Panel estimate = arithmetic mean; score = negative expected squared error. Higher is better. No correction model is fitted.
Paired bootstrap preserves the observed mix of claimed cue sizes; the interval is conditional on this jar and this respondent sample.
The experiment's claimed social group size N is separate from plotted panel size k. These curves average actual reports, not fictitious peers.
